title: Converse Relationship Between nvAE and kess+nAE
summary: The kess property together with nAE security implies nvAE security; whether nvAE implies both, or instead admits a qualified converse or separation, remains open.

formal_statement.body: For authenticated-encryption schemes, satisfying both the $\mathsf{kess}$ property and $\mathsf{nAE}$ security is known to imply $\mathsf{nvAE}$ security. Determine the exact converse relationship: does $\mathsf{nvAE}$ security imply $\mathsf{kess}\land\mathsf{nAE}$, and, if not, what qualification or separation precisely characterizes the reverse direction?

scope.domain: Security relationships among notions for variable-stretch authenticated-encryption schemes.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether nvAE security implies both kess and nAE security; otherwise, characterize the precise qualification or separation in the reverse direction.

progress.summary: The discussion states that Theorem 2 proves kess together with nAE implies nvAE. It explicitly leaves the exact reverse relationship as an open problem.
citation_labels: Reza Reyhanitabar et al., Authenticated Encryption with Variable Stretch
